title: A Log That Cannot Fill the Disk: Rotation Under a Byte Budget, and a Guard Against One Error Said a Million Times

questions.question: Why is a full disk worse than a program that cannot write its log?
options: It stops everything else that writes: the configuration, the black box dump, the next update, temporary files
questions.explanation: Ten different looking faults, one cause.

questions.question: With 10 MB files, 20 files and 200 MB, how much can the log take in the steady state?
options: 200 MB: the smaller of the total and files times file size

questions.question: A day at 100 KB/s fills a 4 GB disk after how long with no limit?
options: 11.1 hours: the robot dies in its first shift
questions.explanation: With the budget the peak was 199 MB.

questions.question: Why is the current file never deleted?
options: Deleting it would lose the record just written: a record bigger than the whole budget is kept until the next one arrives

questions.question: A camera says the same error 1000 times a second for 10 s. How many are written and how many counted?
options: 5 written, 9995 suppressed and counted, handed over once as a summary
questions.explanation: The log grows with the number of different faults.

questions.question: Why does rotation without a guard still lose?
options: The repeated message fills the budget and pushes out the history that explains it, deleted by the fault itself
